Revision item 26 (R3-minor#10). The Fig. 5 recovery rate counts a simulated TE as recovered when a
RepeatMasker hit overlaps it reciprocally by >= 80%. The same RepeatMasker output (four Fig. 3D
scenarios, replicates 1-5) is re-evaluated at 50%, 70%, 80% and 90% reciprocal overlap
(`16_tair10_overlap_threshold_sweep.sh`). Base-pair-level recall and precision, which need no
threshold, are reported in `25.1_item23_28_benchmark_repeatmasker.Rmd`.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
WRK <- "/workspace/cflthc/script/TEgenomeSimulator_publication_code" # clean up this line before git push
SIMOUT <- file.path(WRK, "output")
OUT <- file.path(WRK, "output/tair10_overlap_threshold/")
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = OUT)

scenarios <- 1:4
reps <- 1:5
thresholds <- c(50, 70, 80, 90)
threshold_colors <- c("50%" = "#C6DBEF", "70%" = "#6BAED6", "80%" = "#2171B5", "90%" = "#08306B")

sim_dir <- function(n, i) file.path(SIMOUT, sprintf("TEgenomeSimulator_tair10_sd_scenario%d_rep%d_result", n, i))
```

```{r, load_libraries, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
```

## 1. Load recovery tables

```{r, load_files, echo=FALSE}
read_bins <- function(n, i, eval_dir) {
  read.delim(file.path(sim_dir(n, i), eval_dir, "recovery_by_bin2D.tsv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(scenario = paste0("scenario", n), rep = i)
}
grid <- expand.grid(scenario = scenarios, rep = reps, threshold = thresholds)
bins <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid)), function(k) {
  read_bins(grid$scenario[k], grid$rep[k], paste0("RM_recovery_eval_f", grid$threshold[k])) |>
    dplyr::mutate(threshold = grid$threshold[k])
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(threshold_label = factor(paste0(threshold, "%"), levels = names(threshold_colors)))

# the 80% rerun should reproduce the Fig. 5 evaluation (RM_recovery_eval/)
orig80 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(grid |> dplyr::filter(threshold == 80))), function(k) {
  g <- grid |> dplyr::filter(threshold == 80)
  read_bins(g$scenario[k], g$rep[k], "RM_recovery_eval")
}))
check80 <- dplyr::inner_join(orig80, bins |> dplyr::filter(threshold == 80),
                             by = c("scenario", "rep", "integrity_interval", "identity_interval"),
                             suffix = c("_fig5", "_sweep"))
cat("80% sweep identical to the Fig. 5 evaluation:",
    nrow(check80) == nrow(orig80) && all(check80$total_fig5 == check80$total_sweep) &&
      all(check80$recovered_fig5 == check80$recovered_sweep), "\n")
```

## 2. Overall recovery rate by threshold

```{r, overall, echo=FALSE}
overall_rep <- bins |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, threshold_label, rep) |>
  dplyr::summarise(rate = sum(recovered) / sum(total), .groups = "drop")
overall <- overall_rep |>
  dplyr::group_by(scenario, threshold_label) |>
  dplyr::summarise(rate_mean = mean(rate), rate_sd = sd(rate), .groups = "drop")
kable(overall |> tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = scenario, names_from = threshold_label,
                                    values_from = c(rate_mean, rate_sd), names_vary = "slowest"),
      digits = 3, caption = "Overall recovery rate (pooled over bins) by reciprocal-overlap threshold (mean and SD of 5 replicates).")
write.csv(overall, paste0(OUT, "overlap_threshold_overall.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Saved file name: overlap_threshold_overall.csv

## 3. Recovery by identity and integrity slice

Pooled recovery rate of each identity (or integrity) slice within a replicate, then mean and SD
across replicates, as in the Fig. 5 marginal bar plots. Slices are shown when they contain at least
one simulated TE in every replicate.

```{r, marginals, echo=FALSE}
slice_rate <- function(slice_col, dimension) {
  bins |>
    dplyr::group_by(scenario, threshold_label, rep, slice = .data[[slice_col]]) |>
    dplyr::summarise(total = sum(total), recovered = sum(recovered), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::group_by(scenario, threshold_label, slice) |>
    dplyr::filter(all(total > 0)) |>
    dplyr::summarise(n_mean = mean(total), sd = sd(recovered / total), rate = mean(recovered / total), .groups = "drop") |>
    dplyr::mutate(dimension = dimension)
}
marg <- dplyr::bind_rows(slice_rate("identity_interval", "Identity"), slice_rate("integrity_interval", "Integrity"))
write.csv(marg, paste0(OUT, "overlap_threshold_by_slice.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# change in rate when moving from 80% to 50% or 90%, per slice
marg_delta <- marg |>
  dplyr::select(scenario, dimension, slice, threshold_label, rate) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = threshold_label, values_from = rate) |>
  dplyr::mutate(delta_50_vs_80 = `50%` - `80%`, delta_90_vs_80 = `90%` - `80%`)
kable(marg_delta |> dplyr::group_by(scenario, dimension) |>
        dplyr::summarise(max_gain_at_50 = max(delta_50_vs_80), max_loss_at_90 = min(delta_90_vs_80), .groups = "drop"),
      digits = 3, caption = "Largest change of a slice's recovery rate relative to the 80% threshold.")
write.csv(marg_delta, paste0(OUT, "overlap_threshold_by_slice_delta.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

Saved file names: overlap_threshold_by_slice.csv, overlap_threshold_by_slice_delta.csv

```{r, marginal_plot, echo=FALSE, fig.width = 14, fig.asp = 0.6}
plotwidth <- 14
plotheight <- 8.4
# all ten bins on every panel (empty bins appear as gaps), so panels stay aligned across scenarios;
# the interval strings, e.g. "[0.6-0.7)", sort in bin order and are used as labels
slice_bins <- sort(unique(c(bins$identity_interval, bins$integrity_interval)))

p_marg <- ggplot(marg, aes(x = slice, y = rate, colour = threshold_label, group = threshold_label)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 1.2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = pmax(rate - sd, 0), ymax = pmin(rate + sd, 1)), width = 0.3) +
  facet_grid(dimension ~ scenario) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = threshold_colors, name = "Reciprocal\noverlap") +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = slice_bins) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_text(size = rel(1.1))) +
  labs(x = "Bin (identity in the top row, integrity in the bottom row)",
       y = "Recovery rate")
p_marg
```

```{r, save_marginal_plot, echo=FALSE}
png(filename = paste0(OUT, "overlap_threshold_by_slice.png"), width = plotwidth, height = plotheight, units = "in", res = 1200)
print(p_marg)
while (!is.null(dev.list()))  dev.off()
```

Saved file name: overlap_threshold_by_slice.png

## 4. Notes

- The evaluation is strand- and family-agnostic, as in Fig. 5: any RepeatMasker hit with the
  required reciprocal overlap counts. Family and superfamily accuracy are in
  `25.1_item23_28_benchmark_repeatmasker.Rmd` (scenario 1).
- Lower thresholds accept hits that cover only part of a fragmented copy, or hits that extend well
  beyond it; higher thresholds require nearly exact boundaries.
